source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Choose whichever orientation results in the cleanest connector layout, and [CLIENT_NAME_001] adapt the case to your board.

value_updates.board_orientation_rule: Use whichever board orientation produces the cleanest connector layout, with the enclosure adapted to the board.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
These are some constraints that come to mind:

Constraints that apply in either orientation:
\- Put J\_BAT on a short edge, since the battery sits alongside the PCB
\- Place USB-C on a short edge because it is user-facing
\- Keep the display connectors (J\_DISP\_SPI / J\_DISP\_I2C / J\_DISP\_LED) together on the edge nearest the route for the display flex
\- Point the ESP32-S3 antenna end away from the battery and maintain a ≥3mm keepout

value_updates.battery_connector_location: Place J_BAT on a short edge alongside the battery.
value_updates.usb_c_location: Place USB-C on a short, user-facing edge.
value_updates.display_connector_grouping: Keep J_DISP_SPI, J_DISP_I2C, and J_DISP_LED together on the edge nearest the display-flex route.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Yes, I believe they can. Now that there is only one board + sensors/buttons/leds, which are all easy to position, I don’t think it matters where you place them.

value_updates.general_connector_placement: Connectors may be positioned along the proposed three board sides, with placement otherwise flexible subject to the specified battery, USB-C, and display-connector constraints.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Thanks for sending this. Everything looks good, but I can see only one possible issue. The connector above usb is probably for the battery because it is L shape. Since usb has to pass through an opening in the case, the case would obstruct us from plugging the battery cable into that connector.

execution.observed_behavior: Visual design review showed that the enclosure around the USB opening would obstruct access to the adjacent L-shaped battery connector.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: It looks good now. I think that’s everything. Thanks.

execution.observed_behavior: The client visually approved the revised integrated-board layout after the battery-connector clearance problem was raised.

routing_warnings.description: The clause requiring the ESP32-S3 antenna to face away from the battery with a minimum 3 mm keepout belongs to the separate antenna-clearance Requirement.
This message evaluates components located in the ESP32 antenna clear area and should be routed to the antenna-clearance Requirement.
